about: St. Louis's preconfigured landmarks, written as of 1986.

landmarks.name: Gateway Arch
landmarks.text: Eero Saarinen's 630-foot stainless steel arch on the riverfront, the Gateway to the West. Egg-shaped tram cars ride up inside each leg to a window at the top.

landmarks.name: Busch Stadium
landmarks.text: The round downtown stadium of the Cardinals and the football Cardinals, its rim lined with arches echoing the Gateway. Whitey Herzog's speedsters win on the artificial turf.

landmarks.name: Anheuser-Busch Brewery
landmarks.text: The largest brewery in the world in Soulard, with the Clydesdales in their Victorian stable. The free tour ends in the hospitality room.

landmarks.name: Union Station
landmarks.text: The great Romanesque station, once the busiest in the world, reopened last year as a hotel and shopping mall. Its Grand Hall's whispering arch still works.

landmarks.name: Forest Park
landmarks.text: The 1,300-acre park of the 1904 World's Fair, larger than Central Park, with the zoo, the art museum and the Muny outdoor theatre. Families come for the free museums.

landmarks.name: Saint Louis Art Museum
landmarks.text: Cass Gilbert's Palace of Fine Arts from the 1904 World's Fair, on Art Hill in Forest Park. Sledders take over the hill in winter.

landmarks.name: Saint Louis Zoo
landmarks.text: The free zoo in Forest Park with the 1904 Flight Cage and a miniature railroad. Its chimpanzee show is famous.

landmarks.name: Old Courthouse
landmarks.text: The domed courthouse where Dred Scott sued for his freedom in 1847, framed by the Arch. Slaves were once sold on its steps.

landmarks.name: Eads Bridge
landmarks.text: The 1874 steel arch bridge over the Mississippi, the first of its kind in the world. Trains rumble along its lower deck.

landmarks.name: Fabulous Fox Theatre
landmarks.text: The 1929 Siamese Byzantine movie palace on Grand Boulevard, reopened in 1982 after a lavish restoration. Broadway tours and rock concerts play under its gilded dome.

landmarks.name: Cathedral Basilica
landmarks.text: The Romanesque cathedral on Lindell Boulevard, its interior covered in the largest mosaic collection in the world. The tiles are still being installed.

landmarks.name: Missouri Botanical Garden
landmarks.text: Henry Shaw's garden of 1859, with the geodesic Climatron greenhouse and the largest Japanese garden in North America. The lanterns glow on summer nights.

landmarks.name: Soulard Market
landmarks.text: The 1779 farmers' market of the French and German neighbourhood south of downtown. Mardi Gras here is the second biggest in the country.

landmarks.name: Laclede's Landing
landmarks.text: Nine blocks of cobbled streets and cast-iron warehouses beside the Eads Bridge, reborn as bars and restaurants. The only part of old riverfront St. Louis to survive the Arch.

landmarks.name: SS Admiral
landmarks.text: The streamlined Art Deco excursion boat moored on the levee, a fixture of the riverfront since 1940. Its dances and cruises are fading, and its future is uncertain.

landmarks.name: Blueberry Hill
landmarks.text: The University City pub of jukeboxes and memorabilia on the Delmar Loop, where Chuck Berry drops in to visit. Its burgers are local legend.

landmarks.name: Ted Drewes Frozen Custard
landmarks.find: Ted Drewes Frozen Custard, Chippewa Street
landmarks.text: The custard stand on old Route 66, where the 'concrete' is so thick they hand it over upside down. Lines in the summer heat stretch to the street.

landmarks.name: The Arena
landmarks.text: The barrel-roofed arena by Forest Park where the Blues play, called the Checkerdome for a few years by its pet-food sponsor. The organ plays 'When the Saints Go Marching In'.
